newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 24.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The government goes on the offensive after defeating the farmers: Prime Minister Costas Simitis prepares the deregulation of the market, expansion of the banking system and major changes to the insurance sector.
--A new round of interest rate cuts has been signalled by the finance ministry's decision to reduce interest on its last issue of treasury bills for the year.
--Conservative opposition New Democracy puts its internal party woes on hold for the Christmas-New Year break. Back to the trenches however in early January.

--Most of Greece will be enjoying a white Christmas this year with plummeting temperatures, strong winds and snowfall predicted. Athenians appear to prefer home to village with traffic on the nation's roads reduced.

--Special Edition: Year Zero. If Christ were to be born today, what would be the outcome? UN peacekeepers and television crews converge on the manger - Christ announces his political programme: exclusive interview with 'E' - Prime Minister Costas Simitis says: "There are no Messiahs" - Christ referees in the Israeli-Palestinian play-offs.
--The Turkish press has revealed the involvement of a far-right underworld figure in the violence that resulted in the deaths of two unarmed Greek Cypriots on the island over the summer.
--The Hellenic Navy's report on the sinking of the Kostakos gunboat by a ferryboat off the island of Samos pins blame on an ensign and the ferry's captain but the truth may never be known. TA NEA
--Billions have been lost according to the continuing investigation into the Piraeus fuel scam, where deliveries were made to non-existent vessels and yachts.
--Greeks go into hock in credit card transactions over the holiday break: a record 20 billion drachmas was withdrawn from automatic teller machines over the weekend for Christmas shopping.
--The farmers will get their response in 1998 following talks on a national and world level. Cheaper fuel- one of the demands - will be available at the end of 1997.
